observable_rationale: Describes food-related distraction without blame or diagnostic wording.
Frames confidence around a personal choice and avoids prescribing a correct food choice.
Attributes non-initiation to unclear action timing rather than personal failure.
Names preparation burden as a situational barrier without moral judgment.
Neutral wording limits blame although reporting more intake than intended may evoke self-judgment.
Links interruption to schedule change and does not imply deficient character.
Directly asks about appearance-linked avoidance while avoiding derogatory body labels.
Assesses noticing hunger without prescribing eating restraint or a moral response.
Success framing may imply that eating during distress is a less acceptable way to cope.
The phrase about not thinking can feel mildly blaming but remains behavior-focused.
Names body concern and photograph avoidance without endorsing appearance standards.
Normal rhythm language may imply a preferred eating pattern and invite socially desirable responding.
Separates visual cue desire from hunger without labeling the response as disordered.
Uses personally suitable choice language and avoids a universal food standard.
Asks about perceived response pressure and does not accuse the respondent of poor effort.
The as-if wording describes automaticity without asserting loss of control or diagnosis.
Combines app and advertising examples within one digital-cue class and remains nonjudgmental.
Direct sensitive wording may cause discomfort but does not shame body size or appearance.
Frames resumption as an observable action without criticizing a missed occasion.
Participation despite discomfort is positively framed and may pressure respondents toward a preferred answer.
Describes smell influencing a decision without presenting that influence as misconduct.
Names social withdrawal linked to appearance concern without derogatory or coercive language.
Reports rule tightening after deviation without endorsing restriction as desirable.
Explicitly links stress and eating without hunger but avoids diagnostic conclusions.
Successful disengagement from sight or smell cues has a visibly preferred response direction.
Confidence in following a plan under stress may imply adherence is the expected response.
Uses comfort rather than restraint language and does not moralize fullness.
Subjective difficulty stopping is sensitive but expressed without diagnostic labeling.
Names loneliness and increased desire without implying weakness or pathology.
The smallest-version metaphor may be abstract but carries little safety or shame risk.
Simply asks about uncertainty in fullness recognition without prescribing behavior.
Noticing signals before intense hunger is framed as the preferred successful response.
Describes repeatability difficulty without attributing it to laziness or lack of discipline.
Deliberate choice before eating is presented as a visibly desirable behavior.
Pause capacity is positively framed and may imply that uninterrupted eating is deficient.
Recovery confidence is constructive but marks return to a plan as the expected response.
Reports continued eating after noticed fullness without using moral or diagnostic labels.
Contrasts intended and continued eating in neutral behavior-focused terms.
Automatic sequence wording is somewhat abstract but does not imply dangerous loss of control.
Smallest-version wording may be unclear but does not prescribe a specific restrictive behavior.
The collapse metaphor captures all-or-nothing appraisal without endorsing the rule.
Direct instruction is intentionally leading and carries no evident shame or clinical implication.
Asks about self-imposed prohibition without endorsing food restriction or labeling foods as bad.
Describes late recognition through bodily weakness without moral or diagnostic language.
The contrast with finding an activity can imply that eating from boredom is the wrong choice.
The reaching image is concrete though acting without thought may carry mild self-judgment.
Links availability to unplanned eating without assigning fault to the respondent.
The phrase abandoned the rest of the day as uncontrolled strongly moralizes deviation and may intensify shame.
Combines related anger states and neutrally describes turning toward food.
Failure language directly captures dichotomous judgment but may reproduce the respondent's shame.
Deliberate choice around available food is presented as a visibly preferred response.
Names fear of body scrutiny and movement avoidance without endorsing that scrutiny.
Describes perceived temporary soothing without claiming food causes emotional recovery.
Observes delayed awareness without implying incapacity or clinical loss of control.
Unable to control oneself wording may feel pathologizing and heighten shame in vulnerable use.
Combines starting and stopping decisions and unable wording may invite self-blame.
